# Component Inventory — apps/desktop

*Generated by the BMad document-project workflow — deep scan, 2026-07-17.*

## Overview

`apps/desktop` is an Electron shell — the project's own header comment in [`main.js`](../apps/desktop/main.js) calls it the "viable tier": "No auto-update, no tray, no custom menus — deliberately small." It does not implement any UI components of its own. It forks the packaged Next.js standalone server (built from `apps/web`) as a child process, waits for it to answer HTTP, and points a single `BrowserWindow` at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. Every visible component — sidebar, wheel, dock, cards, dialogs — is the web cockpit rendered inside that window; see [`./component-inventory-web.md`](./component-inventory-web.md) for that inventory.

This file catalogs only what `apps/desktop` itself contributes: the native window/shell configuration in [`main.js`](../apps/desktop/main.js) (479 lines) and [`server-preload.js`](../apps/desktop/server-preload.js) (7 lines). There is no JSX/React, no HTML template, and no renderer-side preload script in this package.

## Shell Surfaces

| Surface | Defined in | Configuration | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main window | `createWindow(url)`, [`main.js:324-347`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L324-L347) | `BrowserWindow({ width: 1280, height: 800, backgroundColor: "#0a0a0a", show: false, title, webPreferences: { contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false } })` | Exactly one window, created on app ready and recreated on macOS `activate` if none remain. Hidden until `ready-to-show`, then shown. Loads the web cockpit via `win.loadURL(url)` — a plain web page, no bespoke chrome beyond title. |
| Window title | `windowTitle()` / `readBuildInfo()`, [`main.js:126-150`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L126-L150); `page-title-updated` handler, [`main.js:339-342`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L339-L342) | `Telar <shortSha>` if a packaged build stamped `build-info.json` (written by `scripts/build-desktop.sh`), else plain `Telar`. | The only bespoke chrome. A `page-title-updated` listener calls `e.preventDefault()` and re-sets the title so the loaded page's own `<title>` can never override the build stamp — this is how a user tells which build they're running. |
| Application menu | — | None defined. | No `Menu.setApplicationMenu()` call anywhere in `main.js`. Electron's platform default menu is left as-is (unmodified). |
| Tray icon | — | None found. | No `Tray` import or usage anywhere in `apps/desktop`. |
| Preload / IPC bridge (renderer) | — | None found. | No `contextBridge`, no `ipcMain`/`ipcRenderer` usage anywhere in `main.js` or `server-preload.js`. The renderer has no exposed native API — it is an ordinary web page under `contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false`. |
| Dialogs (native) | — | None found. | No `dialog.showMessageBox`/`showErrorBox`/`showOpenDialog` etc. anywhere in `main.js`. Failures are logged to console and the app quits (`app.quit()` / `app.exit(1)`), not surfaced via native dialogs. |
| Second-instance handling | `app.on("second-instance", ...)`, [`main.js:446-452`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L446-L452) | Focuses (and un-minimizes) the existing window rather than opening a second one. | Gated by `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`; losing the lock quits immediately. |
| Window-close behavior | `app.on("window-all-closed", ...)`, [`main.js:474-477`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L474-L477) | Sets `app.isQuitting = true` and calls `app.quit()` unconditionally. | Explicitly deviates from macOS convention — the code comment reads "viable tier quits" rather than keeping the app alive in the Dock with zero windows. |
| Server child process (not a UI surface, but the shell's only child) | `startServer(port)`, [`main.js:228-293`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L228-L293) | `fork()`s the standalone `server.js` with `execArgv: ["--require", server-preload.js]` and an `ipc` stdio channel. | `server-preload.js` registers one handler — `process.on("disconnect", () => process.exit(0))` — so the forked server self-exits if the parent Electron process dies for any reason, preventing an orphaned listener against `~/.telar`. Not a rendered surface; listed here because it is the only other process this shell manages. |
| Smoke mode (`--smoke`) | `runSmoke()`, [`main.js:370-434`](../apps/desktop/main.js#L370-L434) | Boots the real server, curls `/`, checks the bundled `@playwright/mcp` CLI and the bundled `claude-agent-sdk` native binary, then exits 0/1. | **Never creates a `BrowserWindow`** — `window-all-closed` is a no-op in this mode and the single-instance lock is never taken. Used as the fail-closed gate in `scripts/build-desktop.sh` after packaging; not a user-facing surface. |

Window defaults (`width`, `height`, `backgroundColor`, `webPreferences`) are the only visual parameters this package controls; there is no theming, no custom titlebar/traffic-light configuration, and no additional `BrowserWindow` instances (e.g. no settings window, no about panel, no splash screen).

## Reuse Guidance

- **There is nothing to reuse here for UI work.** Any feature involving visible components — new panels, dialogs, settings screens, cockpit widgets — belongs in `apps/web` and is documented in [`./component-inventory-web.md`](./component-inventory-web.md). `apps/desktop` has no component library, no styling system, and renders no JSX.
- **If a feature needs native OS integration** (a real system tray, native menu items, OS-level notifications, native open/save dialogs, deep-linking, auto-update), none of that scaffolding exists yet in `apps/desktop` — it would be new work in `main.js`, and per the file's own stated intent ("deliberately small"), such additions should be a deliberate scope decision, not an incidental add.
- **If a feature needs the renderer to call native APIs**, there is currently no `contextBridge`/preload surface exposed to the `BrowserWindow` at all. Adding one is a nontrivial change to the security posture (`contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false` is presently honored with zero exceptions) and should be scoped explicitly rather than bolted on.
- **Build/window-title stamping** (`readBuildInfo()`/`windowTitle()`) is the one piece of desktop-specific "product" behavior in the shell. Any change to how builds are identified to the user should go through `build-info.json` (written by `scripts/build-desktop.sh`) and `windowTitle()` together, not just one side.
- **For architecture/boot-sequence detail** (login-shell env capture, stable-port persistence, standalone server resolution, bundled-binary materialization, packaging) see [`./architecture-desktop.md`](./architecture-desktop.md) — this document intentionally covers only the UI/shell-surface inventory.
